answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph: transition mass is damped at each step, so influence follows supported edges rather than identities. A Sybil cluster shaped like a lantern around a walnut seed, or a spiral of colluding nodes, must cross a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits escape probability and, through spectral min-cut and transitivity bounds, caps aggregate voting weight despite arbitrary internal attestations.
